actually_viewed.source: Montana Ghost Town Preservation Society Bulletin, Spring 2022, printed/PDF page 7; reprint of Ellen Baumler, Boarding House Architecture
observations: Two upper sash windows in horizontal-board false front; broad cornice.
Ground-floor facade has scored plaster and closely spaced timber-framed openings.
French-door/small-pane construction is supported by the accompanying historian’s text.
Merchants, people and pack animals appear in the source photograph; none will be modeled.
limits: Monochrome photograph cannot establish paint colours.
Original exposure date is not provided; early commercial phase is inferred from storefront signage and comparison with the documented later livery conversion, not catalog-dated.
The upper single hayloft door in modern photographs must not replace these two upper windows.

actually_viewed.source: Montana Heritage Commission structural repair report, 2013, PDF page 33
observations: Modern street and rear photographs show rubble masonry, timber upper cladding and gabled rear.
Report documents three original ground-floor stores and an upstairs meeting hall in the 1863 building.
Early-1870s livery conversion enlarged the center entrance and reused a door upstairs.
The committee meeting-site association is explicitly described as popular legend.
limits: Restored barn photographs do not authenticate early store colours or original rear openings.
Red doors, modern signs, flag, concrete pavement, loft door and livery fittings will not be copied as an 1860s reconstruction.

additional_actually_read: NPS Preservation Brief 22, printed pages 3–4: early lime/sand stucco and aggregate-dependent colour.
NPS Preservation Brief 19, printed pages 1–4: dressed wood shingles, regional species, sawn shingles in the nineteenth century.
USDA Ponderosa pine FS-254, Characteristics and Properties: pale sapwood and yellowish to light reddish/orange-brown heartwood.
Montana Historical Society educator article: self-appointed committees outside government; history contested. Specific Plummer date is inconsistent and excluded.
decision: Fictional Montana commercial meeting hall circa 1864–1870, informed by the early facade. Not a replica or authenticated vigilante headquarters. Provisional game name remains unchanged.
